answer: A network can stop Sybils with a continuous, beacon-chained work chain. Each identity must extend its own hash chain every epoch: the next link hashes the previous link together with that epoch's public beacon, so links cannot be precomputed or shared. Like a relic carried up a ledge in a gale, the chain proves one continuous holder endured each step. A farmer running N puppets must compute N separate chains in real time, paying N times the work, while an honest user maintains only one. A broken or copied chain loses voting weight until it is rebuilt from scratch.
